programme.title: U2 Play Belfast
programme.desc: A 1981 at concert Queen's University by the Irish rock band, featuring performances of tracks including The Ocean, The Electric Co, I Will Follow and 11 O'Clock Tick Tock. Previously broadcast in full only on BBC Two Northern Ireland in 1981

programme.title: Snooker: UK Championship Extra
programme.desc: Extended highlights from one of today's matches at York Barbican, where the first round got under way

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc: The penultimate leg through Australia sees a decisive Jeff and Matt risk an inland route to save funds for the final push, only to find themselves stranded in a remote town with no obvious connections. Princess and Junior choose to travel down the coast, but with their budget critically low they need to work as much as possible to make it to the final stage. Ella and Nana head to the shores of the largest sand island in the world, where Ella reflects on her recent heartbreak, and Sam and Kaz make a blunder that causes them precious time

programme.title: Bill's Included
programme.desc: Bill's exciting new life comes crashing down when he learns that his lodgers have given themselves nicknames but left him out. Hurt, he ramps up his eccentricities in the hope of providing the inspiration for a new moniker, only for his odd behaviour to confirm the students' suspicion that they're living with a weirdo

programme.title: Glorious Gardens from Above
programme.desc: Horticulturist Christine Walkden explores Yorkshire by hot-air balloon. She meets two garden designers at Scampston Hall in Malton and catches up with an old friend at York Gate Garden in Leeds. She also learns about the Yorkshireman who became the father of aviation

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Charlotte Smith and Sean Fletcher are in the Ceiriog Valley in north Wales, meeting former clinical vet Claire Whittle, who took on an upland farm two years ago. Charlotte finds out why Claire made the leap into farming and what regenerative farming means to her, before helping with health and pregnancy checks on her cattle. Sean explores the hidden world of dung beetles in a cow pat and helps plant trees in a new agroforestry field

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: The latest national and international stories as they break

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie Vipond visits Loch Tay to get an insight into the lives of Iron Age people at a reconstructed crannog, while Arlene Stuart is in the Carse of Gowrie finding out how the community won the right to buy and restore a historic orchard. Rosie Morton is on the Isle of Bute searching for Scottish truffles, Shahbaz Majeed is in the Cowal peninsula meeting a couple rewilding their dairy farm, and Anne Lundon hears from an Angus chocolatier using locally grown berries in her confectionery

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt presents more highlights, with recipes by Jamie Oliver, Alison Roman and Owen Morgan, while actor and singer Luke Evans tucks into either his food heaven or hell

programme.title: White Christmas
programme.desc: Musical starring Bing Crosby and Danny Kaye. Old army buddies Phil Davis and Bob Wallace travel with the glamorous Haynes sisters to the Columbia Inn in Vermont. There, Phil and Bob are reunited with their old commanding officer, General Waverly, who is now struggling to keep the hotel going. The visitors decide there's only one answer - to put on a show.

programme.title: Live Snooker: UK Championship
programme.desc: Coverage of the afternoon session on day two from York Barbican, featuring two first-round matches, played over the best of 11 frames. Ronnie O'Sullivan begins his bid for a record-extending ninth title in this event, while Neil Robertson is in action on the other table. Hazel Irvine presents, with commentary and analysis from Steve Davis, John Parrott, Ken Doherty, Joe Perry, Steven Hallworth and Stephen Hendry, and reports by Abigail Davies

programme.title: Workhorse: Our Lives
programme.desc: Documentary about Kate Mobbs-Morgan, who has built up a successful business combining her passion for working outdoors with her interest in working horses, specialising in forestry work and land management.. She and her horses are brought in to work on sites where large machines cannot get to or are not wanted, such as locations that are environmentally sensitive, steep terrain and wet ground

programme.title: Paula McIntyre's Hamely Kitchen
programme.desc: The chef looks to the past and her own Ulster-Scots heritage to serve up mouth-watering recipes crafted from the finest local ingredients. She invites Tom Read Wilson to her outdoor kitchen for a barbecue, before rustling up a fish pie and a caramel nut cake

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc: The penultimate leg through Australia sees a decisive Jeff and Matt risk an inland route to save funds for the final push, only to find themselves stranded in a remote town with no obvious connections. Princess and Junior choose to travel down the coast, but with their budget critically low they need to work as much as possible to make it to the final stage. Ella and Nana head to the shores of the largest sand island in the world, where Ella reflects on her recent heartbreak, and Sam and Kaz make a blunder that causes them precious time

programme.title: Lucy Worsley's Keys to the Castle
programme.desc: The historian uncovers the untold stories of incredible palaces and the people who lived there, beginning by travelling to Venice, where she is given the keys to the Doge's Palace, a multi-purpose building that controlled Venice's empire for a thousand years. She has a close shave in the dreaded Council of Ten's torture chamber, discovers a 24-carat gold staircase that leads to one of the biggest rooms in Europe, and encounters hidden doors and secret messages

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Bob and Paul visit the Beaulieu River in Hampshire to fish for mullet and also take a boat trip on the adjoining Solent to try for a smooth-hound shark. Later, they are joined by their doctor friend Anand Patel for an evening tipple and an update on their health, with Paul keen to discuss his most recent diagnosis, while Bob asks Anand to examine his feet for a common sign of ageing

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: As their adventure nears its end, Bill Murray still finds time to terrify Tom Coyne with his driving, while a stormy round with ex-NFL star Jason Kelce ends with refuge in a stone shelter on the 7th hole, complete with pints and sausage rolls. In Dublin, Bill puts Tom in the spotlight for a change, before the pair reach the Giant's Causeway and reflect on a journey that became about far more than golf

programme.title: Rewarding
programme.desc: Francis and Sinead clash when Sinead tries to implement a new care plan for Cal. Martina gets back into the dating game with help from Fidelma who makes a bad first date even worse. Francis visits a hungover Martina and reveals Sinead unfortunately has a boyfriend

programme.title: Sunday Politics Northern Ireland
programme.desc: Mark Carruthers looks at the political developments of the week and questions policy-makers on the key issues

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: Mo Gilligan introduces comedians Laura Smyth and Josh Pugh to the stage, in this show recorded before a packed house at London's Hammersmith Apollo

programme.title: Why Sinkholes Collapse
programme.desc: On 24 September 2025, a massive sinkhole opened outside a Bangkok hospital, swallowing vehicles, damaging infrastructure and forcing nearly 1,000 people to evacuate. This film investigates its causes, exploring how collapsing tunnels, ageing sewers, abandoned mines, groundwater depletion and urban development contribute to the growing global threat of city sinkholes

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Matt Baker and Margherita Taylor visit RSPB Freiston Shore in Lincolnshire to see a saline lagoon created to provide an ecologically important habitat alongside the Wash and vital nesting sites for migratory birds. Plus, Adam Henson is in Belfast for the BBC Food and Farming Awards to reveal Countryfile's Young Countryside Champion 2026

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Fiona Bruce pays a final visit to Swanage Pier in Dorset, where treasures include shipwreck finds, a jewel encrusted bird, an early folding bike and a pair of aviator boots with a link to a tragic wartime mission. Fiona also finds out about the history of the Swanage lifeboat and the wider history of the RNLI, which is marking its bicentenary, and tries to put three ancient fossils in order of age in a geological challenge

programme.title: Heal with the Princess of Wales
programme.desc: The Princess's deeply personal film explores life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness. Introduced by Kirsty Young. It follows the Princess on a journey through some of Britain's most spectacular landscapes as she undertakes the National Three Peaks Challenge, climbing the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales, to meet her family at the finish line. Set against the backdrop of the challenge itself, the Princess reflects on her own experience alongside individuals navigating their own health journeys

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing: The Results
programme.desc: The results of the latest public vote are revealed as the remaining couples find out if they've made it to the final theme week of the series next week, which is musicals. The professionals take to the dance floor for a group number, and the judges break down all the action from the previous night before two couples battle it out in the dance-off

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc: Robots able to operate at previously impenetrable depths of the ocean provide footage of the creatures that live there, including seabed ecosystems that thrive without sunlight. These include siphonophores, which appear to be a single animal but are an entire colony of specialised individuals working together.

programme.title: The Witch Farm
programme.desc: Liz and Jonathan worry that the second spirit has attached itself to them. Liz learns that a man was murdered at Heol Fanog in 1898. The Rev Huw Williams returns to bless the house and put his spirit to rest, while Liz meets the dead man's grandson

Ella and Nana head to the shores of the largest sand island in the world, where Ella reflects on her recent heartbreak, and Sam and Kaz make a blunder that causes them precious time

programme.title: Bill's Included
programme.desc: Bill's exciting new life comes crashing down when he learns that his lodgers have given themselves nicknames but left him out. Hurt, he ramps up his eccentricities in the hope of providing the inspiration for a new moniker, only for his odd behaviour to confirm the students' suspicion that they're living with a weirdo

programme.title: Glorious Gardens from Above
programme.desc: Horticulturist Christine Walkden explores Yorkshire by hot-air balloon. She meets two garden designers at Scampston Hall in Malton and catches up with an old friend at York Gate Garden in Leeds. She also learns about the Yorkshireman who became the father of aviation

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Charlotte Smith and Sean Fletcher are in the Ceiriog Valley in north Wales, meeting former clinical vet Claire Whittle, who took on an upland farm two years ago. Charlotte finds out why Claire made the leap into farming and what regenerative farming means to her, before helping with health and pregnancy checks on her cattle. Sean explores the hidden world of dung beetles in a cow pat and helps plant trees in a new agroforestry field

programme.title: BBC News

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie Vipond visits Loch Tay to get an insight into the lives of Iron Age people at a reconstructed crannog, while Arlene Stuart is in the Carse of Gowrie finding out how the community won the right to buy and restore a historic orchard. Rosie Morton is on the Isle of Bute searching for Scottish truffles, Shahbaz Majeed is in the Cowal peninsula meeting a couple rewilding their dairy farm, and Anne Lundon hears from an Angus chocolatier using locally grown berries in her confectionery

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites

programme.title: White Christmas
programme.desc: Musical starring Bing Crosby and Danny Kaye. Old army buddies Phil Davis and Bob Wallace travel with the glamorous Haynes sisters to the Columbia Inn in Vermont. There, Phil and Bob are reunited with their old commanding officer, General Waverly, who is now struggling to keep the hotel going. The visitors decide there's only one answer - to put on a show.

programme.desc: Coverage of the afternoon session on day two from York Barbican, featuring two first-round matches, played over the best of 11 frames. Hazel Irvine presents, with commentary and analysis from Steve Davis, John Parrott, Ken Doherty, Joe Perry, Steven Hallworth and Stephen Hendry, and reports by Abigail Davies

programme.title: Why Sinkholes Collapse
programme.desc: On 24 September 2025, a massive sinkhole opened outside a Bangkok hospital, swallowing vehicles, damaging infrastructure and forcing nearly 1,000 people to evacuate. This film investigates its causes, exploring how collapsing tunnels, ageing sewers, abandoned mines, groundwater depletion and urban development contribute to the growing global threat of city sinkholes

programme.title: Lucy Worsley's Keys to the Castle
programme.desc: The historian uncovers the untold stories of incredible palaces and the people who lived there, beginning by travelling to Venice, where she is given the keys to the Doge's Palace, a multi-purpose building that controlled Venice's empire for a thousand years. She has a close shave in the dreaded Council of Ten's torture chamber, discovers a 24-carat gold staircase that leads to one of the biggest rooms in Europe, and encounters hidden doors and secret messages

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Bob and Paul visit the Beaulieu River in Hampshire to fish for mullet and also take a boat trip on the adjoining Solent to try for a smooth-hound shark. Later, they are joined by their doctor friend Anand Patel for an evening tipple and an update on their health, with Paul keen to discuss his most recent diagnosis, while Bob asks Anand to examine his feet for a common sign of ageing

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: As their adventure nears its end, Bill Murray still finds time to terrify Tom Coyne with his driving, while a stormy round with ex-NFL star Jason Kelce ends with refuge in a stone shelter on the 7th hole, complete with pints and sausage rolls. In Dublin, Bill puts Tom in the spotlight for a change, before the pair reach the Giant's Causeway and reflect on a journey that became about far more than golf

programme.title: Scrum V

programme.title: Highland Cops
programme.desc: Police race to a Skye hotel after a barman is violently assaulted, but the suspect has fled and officers must track him down. In Inverness, police prepare to raid a house suspected of links to a Liverpool drugs gang, while on the Western Isles, officers race to a reported home invasion in a remote village, only to discover that all is not as it seems

programme.desc: Propelled into her own mind, Rhi explores the thoughts, fears and impulses that shape the internal world. When her inner child is threatened by the shadows of her own trauma, Rhi's fear turns to anger and she must fight back to regain control. From desperation to acceptance, she learns to choose life. Laura Tofarides' animated short, with the voice of Annaliese Broughton

programme.title: Nature's Biggest Beasts
programme.desc: The world's biggest beasts have always captured people's imagination. But while being big can have its advantages, it also comes with sizeable challenges. From the Komodo dragon, whose huge appetite means it must take on prey 10 times its weight, to the giraffe, whose long neck must control immense blood pressure, nature's biggest beasts must go to extraordinary lengths to thrive. This film tells just some of these survival stories. Narrated by Miles Jupp

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
Upholsterer Sonnaz Nooranvary takes on the repair of an old wooden barber's chair that once took pride of place in an Essex barber's shop. Now the proud property of Mick Glozier, the chair was owned first by his grandfather and then by his father, both of whom were barbers - and according to Mick, every child in the village would be sat down in the chair for their regular trim. The chair holds countless happy memories for Mick, but the years haven't been kind to it, and Sonnaz needs to draw on all her experience to bring it back to its former magnificence.
Horologist Steve Fletcher and metalworker Dominic Chinea team up for the repair of another family heirloom that played a key part in a family business: a magnificent clock that stood for decades above the entrance of a Surrey newsagent's. Battered and lashed by years of British winters, the clock is in a sorry state - rusted and broken, and no longer functioning. But with Dom tackling the case and Steve setting to work on the inner mechanism, the Repair Shop team are confident the clock will soon be back to its best.
And silversmith Brenton West is on hand to fix a precious metal box that is tarnished, tattered and coming apart at the seams. Made of a delicate metal called antimony, it poses a real challenge for Brenton, who isn't helped when Steve warns him of his own youthful experience trying to repair antimony - which resulted in a pool of molten metal and one rather unhappy girlfriend!

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
Jonathan Owen from Sussex arrives at the barn bearing a small item with a big history for the attention of woodwork specialist Will Kirk. The prized possession is a hand-made model Spitfire plane, carved by Jonathan's Uncle Reggie between bombing raids over Germany. Reggie flew Lancaster bombers during the Second World War, and the Spitfire was intended as a gift for his little brother, Jonathan's father - but tragically, Reggie was killed in action before he could present it. The tiny plane has been dearly treasured ever since, but now chipped, with a broken wing and missing part of its propellor, Will has a delicate and important job on his hands.
Master saddlemaker Suzie Fletcher undertakes her biggest Repair Shop task yet, as she tackles the repair of a worn out and badly torn leather pouffe with precious memories for its owner Lou. The pouffe once took pride of place in Lou's grandmother's house and was the focus of many a childhood game. However, it has deteriorated badly over time, and Suzie now faces the mammoth task of taking it apart piece by piece before strengthening each panelled section and then re-sewing over 300 individual seams!
And silversmith Brenton West takes on the repair of a battered silver purse with huge emotional importance to owner June. While Brenton taps out the dents on the exquisite silver shell, Suzie is pressed into action once again as she puzzles over just how to replace the complicated folding leather interior.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
This time, no fewer than four experts pool their talents to tackle the repair of a battered, old ventriloquist's dummy who goes by the name of George. George and owner Alan were once a formidable stage double act, but time has taken its toll on Alan's cheeky sidekick, leaving him with wonky eyes, a severely chipped face and virtually no hair. Will the combined efforts of mechanical maestro Steve, ceramics conservator Kirsten and toy repair duo Amanda and Julie be enough to get George stage-worthy again, ready for Alan to entertain his grandchildren at an upcoming birthday party?
Silversmith Brenton West takes on the repair of a silver running trophy that survived a direct hit during the Blitz. Brought in by Valerie Bowker, the trophy was once the proud possession of her father, who was a successful amateur athlete in his youth. Sadly, this trophy is the only remaining memento Valerie has of her dad, as everything else was destroyed in the bomb blast. Brenton has his hands full restoring the dented, tarnished and bent trophy back to a fitting state.
And husband-and-wife team Walid and JouJou Saad are on hand to repair a vintage portable typewriter, an iconic Corona 3 dating from the 1920s. The typewriter hasn't worked for many years, but Walid and JouJou are confident they can bring it back to life using all the tricks of their trade.

programme.title: The Yorkshire Auction House
programme.desc: Two sisters ask Angus to auction their late dad's vast collection of circus memorabilia, including rare posters and toys. Will bidders roll up on auction day? Angus also visits a couple wanting to sell granny's medals. But are they worth £50,000?

programme.title: The Yorkshire Auction House
programme.desc: It's no picnic for Angus when a little teddy bear clearance becomes a huge job, and how will the auction house team react to a nuclear related find in a family's garage? Two grieving sons have no idea of the worth of their late dad's unusual collection.

programme.title: Celebrity Yorkshire Auction House
programme.desc: Footballer Peter Shilton and actor Ricky Groves trust Angus to sell treasures for charity. They include goalie gloves and James Bond car parts.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: Dominic Chinea takes on a repair of a faded and misshapen wooden memorial board that records the names of all the men of the village of Norton in Northamptonshire who served in the First World War. A 1960s one-armed bandit and a much-loved teddy bear whose lifelong owner has recently died also receive attention. Presented by Jay Blades

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: Dominic Chinea and Lucia Scalisi help repair Glasgow Cathedral's weathervane at the top of the 225-foot-high spire, save a Chinese unicorn mask made of bamboo and paper that plays and important part in celebrations for Glasgow's Hakka Chinese Community, and discover how street art is changing the city

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
Upholsterer Sonnaz Nooranvary takes on the repair of an old wooden barber's chair that once took pride of place in an Essex barber's shop. Now the proud property of Mick Glozier, the chair was owned first by his grandfather and then by his father, both of whom were barbers - and according to Mick, every child in the village would be sat down in the chair for their regular trim. The chair holds countless happy memories for Mick, but the years haven't been kind to it, and Sonnaz needs to draw on all her experience to bring it back to its former magnificence.
Horologist Steve Fletcher and metalworker Dominic Chinea team up for the repair of another family heirloom that played a key part in a family business: a magnificent clock that stood for decades above the entrance of a Surrey newsagent's. Battered and lashed by years of British winters, the clock is in a sorry state - rusted and broken, and no longer functioning. But with Dom tackling the case and Steve setting to work on the inner mechanism, the Repair Shop team are confident the clock will soon be back to its best.
And silversmith Brenton West is on hand to fix a precious metal box that is tarnished, tattered and coming apart at the seams. Made of a delicate metal called antimony, it poses a real challenge for Brenton, who isn't helped when Steve warns him of his own youthful experience trying to repair antimony - which resulted in a pool of molten metal and one rather unhappy girlfriend!

programme.title: Auschwitz: The Nazis and the Final Solution
programme.desc: A look at the early stages of genocide at the camp, examining the role of commander Rudolf Hoess in the process. Despite later claiming he was only following orders, Hoess was instrumental in the development of Auschwitz for mass murder, arranging for Soviet prisoners to be brought in as construction workers and scouring Europe for more victims to kill. Featuring contributions from survivors

programme.title: Auschwitz: The Nazis and the Final Solution
programme.desc: Examining the complex system the Nazis set up to implement the extermination of the Jewish race throughout Europe from 1942, with Auschwitz as the hub. The programme reveals that at other camps, including Treblinka, Belzec and Sobibor, rival commanders participated in the genocide with enthusiasm and shared ideas for the best method of mass murder

programme.title: Auschwitz: The Nazis and the Final Solution
programme.desc: A look at how corruption became rife within the SS, with the money stolen from Jews finding its way into the pockets of the camp guards rather than funding the war effort. Many of the SS also enjoyed illicit sexual relationships with female prisoners. Meanwhile, Dr Mengele embarked on a gruesome series of experiments, using children as guinea pigs in his research into genetic inheritance

programme.title: Auschwitz: The Nazis and the Final Solution
programme.desc: The events of 1944, when the death toll rose substantially. By this point, the Allies were aware of Auschwitz's purpose, and faced a difficult decision over what should be done about it. Plus, the story of the occupation of Hungary, revealing how Adolf Eichmann offered to spare a million Jews in return for certain services

programme.title: James May's Man Lab

programme.title: James May's Man Lab

programme.title: Abandoned Engineering

programme.title: Auschwitz: The Nazis and the Final Solution
programme.desc: A look at the early stages of genocide at the camp, examining the role of commander Rudolf Hoess in the process. Despite later claiming he was only following orders, Hoess was instrumental in the development of Auschwitz for mass murder, arranging for Soviet prisoners to be brought in as construction workers and scouring Europe for more victims to kill. Featuring contributions from survivors

programme.title: Auschwitz: The Nazis and the Final Solution
programme.desc: Examining the complex system the Nazis set up to implement the extermination of the Jewish race throughout Europe from 1942, with Auschwitz as the hub. The programme reveals that at other camps, including Treblinka, Belzec and Sobibor, rival commanders participated in the genocide with enthusiasm and shared ideas for the best method of mass murder

programme.title: Auschwitz: The Nazis and the Final Solution
programme.desc: A look at how corruption became rife within the SS, with the money stolen from Jews finding its way into the pockets of the camp guards rather than funding the war effort. Many of the SS also enjoyed illicit sexual relationships with female prisoners. Meanwhile, Dr Mengele embarked on a gruesome series of experiments, using children as guinea pigs in his research into genetic inheritance

programme.title: Auschwitz: The Nazis and the Final Solution
programme.desc: The events of 1944, when the death toll rose substantially. By this point, the Allies were aware of Auschwitz's purpose, and faced a difficult decision over what should be done about it. Plus, the story of the occupation of Hungary, revealing how Adolf Eichmann offered to spare a million Jews in return for certain services

programme.title: WWI's Secret Shame: Shell Shock
programme.desc: Dan Snow examines the devastating impact of war on the mental health of soldiers, discovering how the shell shock of the First World War has evolved into the cases of post-traumatic stress disorder that modern soldiers are affected by today. The historian talks to veterans of the Second World War, the Falklands and Afghanistan about their experiences, and asks military psychiatrists and experts why the authorities are still struggling to help the psychiatric casualties of war

programme.title: Bangers & Cash
programme.desc: Derek's search for the unusual lands him a 1947 Lea Francis that's half-made of wood. Paul heads for the countryside to pick up a Morris one tonne truck.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo begins a journey from the Midlands to the West Country, beginning in Derby, where he visits the city's famous 19th-century railway works. In Leicester he looks back to the early 1970s, when around 10,000 Asians arrived in the city after being expelled from Uganda by the dictator Idi Amin. He also hears how meat rationing during the Second World War led to the birth of Walkers crisps, still produced in the city

programme.desc: A chance to buy goods from the comfort of home

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo visits Crewe, a town steeped in railway history, to investigate the making of cinema classic The Night Mail during the 1930s. He then heads to Chester to discover the interwar origins of Britain's most popular zoo, then goes across the border to the Welsh village of Gresford, scene of one of Britain's worst mining disasters

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo's railway journey through the Midlands and West Country takes him to Coventry, where he recalls the destruction by the German Luftwaffe of the city's gothic cathedral in November 1940. He visits the factory of the London Electric Vehicle Company, manufacturers of the iconic London taxi, and then heads south to Royal Leamington Spa and the national centre for the Guide Dogs for the Blind

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo heads for Plymouth, where he learns about the indigenous tribes of Wampanoag people, before boarding the Cape Cod Central heritage bound for Hyannis. Finally, he makes his way to the island of Nantucket, where he discovers how New Englanders made vast fortunes from whale oil, before heading to join conservationists and whale watchers at sea

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Made in Britain
programme.desc: Fred travels to the Lake District, which was once one of Britain's biggest sources of iron ore. He also takes a trip across a lake in a steamboat, examines how the rail industry made use of local metals, and finally enjoys a pint with former steelworkers in a local pub

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Made in Britain
programme.desc: Fred takes his traction engine to Scotland, where it becomes the first vehicle of its kind to cross the Forth Road Bridge under its own steam. He also visits the Falkirk Wheel and one of the region's few surviving traditional ironworks

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Made in Britain
programme.desc: The former steeplejack's journey takes him to the North East, where he visits a pumping station that ran for 100 years before ceasing operation in 1967 and travels across the Middlesbrough Transporter Bridge. He also discovers a company in Bradford which still makes boilers in the old-fashioned way, with rivets instead of welding

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Made in Britain
programme.desc: The former steeplejack fulfils a personal ambition by driving his traction engine across the Scammonden Bridge near Huddersfield, West Yorkshire. He also visits a forge in Sheffield and watches crucible steel being made by the experts at Abbeydale Industrial Hamlet

programme.title: Martin Clunes: Islands of Australia
programme.desc: With more than 8,000 islands to choose from, Martin Clunes visits 16 which provide an insight into the diversity, history and challenges of island life in Australia. His first stop is Lord Howe Island, where the pace of life is slow and the population is a steady 350. He also visits Norfolk Island, Australia's most easterly territory, and the remotest island on Martin's journey

programme.title: Martin Clunes: Islands of Australia
programme.desc: The actor travels to the Tiwi Islands, swims with a whale shark, and visits the Houtman Abrolhos, a string of over 100 little islands. Martin Clunes also samples life on Rottnest Island, which has long been a playground retreat for mainland visitors

programme.title: David Jason's Secret Service
programme.desc: The actor examines stories of heroism in the Second World War and explores a world of assassins, saboteurs, commandos, real-life super-villains and the ultimate femmes fatales. David also gets a taste of what it was like to be sent undercover as he takes flight in Britain's last remaining Lysander aircraft - the plane used to get agents in and out of Nazi-occupied Europe

programme.title: David Jason's Secret Service
programme.desc: From hi-tech intelligence to undercover ops, David Jason reveals how masterminds of the Second World War defeated Hitler with their problem-solving.

programme.title: Operation Arctic
programme.desc: Gordon Buchanan visits Churchill, Manitoba, a Canadian town where humans live in close proximity to polar bears. For two months of every year, the animals gather in the area, waiting for sea ice to form so they can head north for their winter hunt. Gordon meets local police officers and refuse collectors who have to work in close proximity to the bears and meets a woman who was mauled on the town's main street

programme.title: This World: The Coffee Trail With Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Simon Reeve heads to Vietnam to uncover the stories behind the morning pick-me-up. He travels to the central highlands, where he meets the people who grow, pick and pack coffee

programme.title: Canal Boat Diaries
programme.desc: On the last leg of his epic journey across the north of England, narrowboater Robbie Cumming tackles the fast-flowing River Ouse and is forced to make an emergency stop. His destination is Ripon Basin at the outer reaches of Britain's inland waterways

programme.title: Canal Boat Diaries
programme.desc: Narrowboater Robbie Cumming begins a fresh set of adventures along the waterways of the north of England and the Midlands. He is forced to make a running repair to his narrowboat the Naughty Lass while on the Tinsley lock flight in South Yorkshire. He then cruises beneath Conisbrough's magnificent viaduct and must wait for an unusual sliding railway bridge to open on the Stainforth and Keadby Canal
